title: Prague, Vienna and Budapest by Train

bestPeriod.window: April to June, September to October, and December for the markets
bestPeriod.avoid: Mid-July to August heat and peak hostel prices

accommodation.note: Hostels and budget hotels, six nights

transport.note: Three trains booked ahead, city transport

activities.note: Opera standing place, thermal bath, castles

profile.difficultyNote: 1/5, city walking and three train rides of 1 to 4 hours

gatewayAirport: PRG Prague, 35 min to the centre by bus and metro; home from BUD Budapest
summary: Four capitals, three easy trains and no car. Prague for its bridges and beer, Vienna for coffee houses and a €15 opera ticket, Bratislava for an afternoon on the Danube and Budapest for its thermal baths. Booked a few weeks ahead, every train costs less than a taxi to the airport.
hook: Four capitals in seven days, three trains for under €60 booked ahead.

itinerary.title: Prague old town
itinerary.morning: Bus 59 and metro from the airport, about 35 minutes. Walk to Old Town Square for the astronomical clock.
itinerary.afternoon: Charles Bridge and the Lesser Town lanes below the castle.
itinerary.evening: Dinner and a 0.5 l Pilsner for under €3 in a Vinohrady beer hall.

itinerary.title: Prague Castle and Petřín
itinerary.morning: Prague Castle grounds and St Vitus nave are free to walk; the combined ticket is optional.
itinerary.afternoon: Down through the gardens to Petřín hill and its mirror maze, then the river.
itinerary.evening: Jazz in a cellar, or the Dancing House terrace at sunset.
itinerary.dayStats: City walking, about 10 km, 130 m up

itinerary.title: Railjet to Vienna
itinerary.morning: Railjet from Prague hlavní nádraží to Vienna in about 4 hours, from €20 booked ahead.
itinerary.afternoon: Check in, then Naschmarkt for a late lunch.
itinerary.evening: Standing place at the Vienna State Opera, from about €15, sold 80 minutes before curtain.

itinerary.title: Vienna, palaces and coffee
itinerary.morning: Schönbrunn gardens and the Gloriette, free; the palace tour is extra.
itinerary.afternoon: The Hofburg and the Museum quarter, then cake in a classic café.
itinerary.evening: Heuriger wine tavern in Grinzing by tram 38.

itinerary.title: Bratislava on the way
itinerary.morning: Regional train to Bratislava in about 1 h, around €12 return-free single.
itinerary.afternoon: Bratislava Castle, the old town and the UFO bridge over the Danube; leave bags in station lockers.
itinerary.evening: Evening train on to Budapest, about 2 h 30 min, from €15.

itinerary.title: Budapest baths and bridges
itinerary.morning: Széchenyi thermal baths in the city park, about €30 for the day.
itinerary.afternoon: Heroes' Square and Andrássy út back to the Parliament on the river.
itinerary.evening: Ruin bars of the Jewish quarter.

itinerary.title: Buda Castle, then home
itinerary.morning: Funicular or the stairs to Buda Castle and Fisherman's Bastion.
itinerary.afternoon: Bus 100E to the airport, about 35 minutes.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hostel in Prague
accommodationStrategy.description: Pick one within walking distance of the main station for the morning train.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €18 to €30 a dorm bed, €60 to €90 a private double

accommodationStrategy.name: Budget hotel in Vienna
accommodationStrategy.location: Vienna, near the Westbahnhof or Hauptbahnhof
accommodationStrategy.description: Vienna's hostels are large and clean; budget hotels near the stations are close in price for two.
accommodationStrategy.priceNote: €25 to €40 a dorm bed, €80 to €120 a double

accommodationStrategy.name: Hostel in Budapest
accommodationStrategy.description: The Jewish quarter is the hostel quarter, steps from the ruin bars.

logistics.connectivity: EU roaming works in all four countries.
logistics.weather: Danube summers are hot and continental; spring and autumn are best for walking.
logistics.bookingWindows: Railjet and EuroCity fares rise as the date nears; book 3 to 6 weeks ahead on the operators' sites.
logistics.money: Three currencies: koruna, euro, forint. Cards work almost everywhere; skip exchange booths.
logistics.transportRules: An Interrail Global pass rarely pays for three short trains; buy point to point.
logistics.gettingThere: Fly into Prague and out of Budapest; open-jaw tickets often cost the same as a return.

proTips: Use the station lockers in Bratislava hlavná stanica so the stopover costs nothing but time.
Buy the Vienna 24 or 48 hour transport ticket only if you plan more than four rides a day.

raw.Who It Suits: First trips by train, couples, friends, families with older children

typeSpecific.transitPass: Point-to-point tickets beat a pass for this route

packingNotes: A day bag for the Bratislava stop
Flip-flops and a towel for the baths
A smart layer for the opera
whatCouldGoWrong: Track work can replace a train with a bus on Sundays; check the operator's site the day before.

highlights.title: Charles Bridge at dawn
highlights.line: Prague's Gothic bridge before the crowds, statues against the castle.

highlights.title: €15 at the opera
highlights.line: Standing places at the Vienna State Opera, sold on the night.

highlights.title: Széchenyi baths
highlights.line: Outdoor thermal pools in a palace, steaming even in winter.

highlights.title: Bratislava Castle
highlights.line: A Danube capital in an afternoon between two trains.
